works.abstract: The rise of microplastics (MPs) in the environment has raised concerns about their potential impact on human health. Recent research has revealed interactions between MPs and the gut microbiome, with new evidence suggesting that chronic MP exposure may contribute to obesity and metabolic dysfunction, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This review aims to provide an overview of our current understanding of MPs from animal models, human studies, and interventions, and to explain how they disrupt gut microbial homeostasis and cause metabolic diseases. Currently, what is known so far suggests that MPs can disrupt the gut microbiome, which, in turn, can increase intestinal permeability and trigger systemic inflammation. Inflammation has downstream effects on lipid and glucose metabolism and hepatic pathology. However, gaps remain in our understanding of the dose-response effects or efficacy of any intervention. We identified critical research gaps and showed that targeting the gut microbiome may help prevent MP-induced metabolic disorders.
works.title: Microplastics, Gut Microbiome and Obesity: A Narrative Review of Emerging Links and Mechanisms
